name: Csilla Owusu-Nazarov
role: Organ harvester and procurement specialist working the margins of legitimate medical infrastructure
location: South Deering Sump — operates out of a converted cold-storage unit adjacent to the Aurochs Medical Complex overflow lots, near Armitage and Milwaukee
description:
Csilla is medium height and deceptively slight, with Hungarian-Ghanaian features — warm brown skin, heavy-lidded dark eyes, wide mouth usually set in a neutral expression that people keep reading as a smile. Their cat ears are geneware, common enough, but theirs are the mottled grey-and-amber of an actual South African wildcat — chosen deliberately for the unsettling accuracy. They keep their natural hair in tight, small braids, always pinned up under a surgical cap during work. They smell faintly of antiseptic even when they're not working, a smell that has become so much a part of them that they no longer notice it.

Csilla trained for three years in Aurochs Medical Complex's licensed surgical technician program before washing out for reasons listed on their record as 'professional conduct irregularities' and in reality involving a confrontation with a senior tech over the disposal of viable organs from unconsenting deceased patients — a confrontation in which Csilla was technically wrong but morally, they believe, correct. They moved laterally into independent procurement within six months. They are not sadistic, not cavalier, and not in any way comfortable with what they do — but they have concluded, through a logic they can walk you through step by step, that there is a demand, there is a supply, and the official channels are too slow and too expensive for the people who need them most. They charge on a sliding scale they invented themselves.

core_fears: that the ethical framework they've built is self-serving rationalization
causing a patient's death through their own error
core_desires: to give people access to medical care the system has priced out of their reach
to be believed when they say they're trying to do something good
coping_mechanisms: exhaustive self-justifying ethical frameworks maintained like the cold-storage unit — meticulously
treating every procedure as a case study, emotional distance through technical focus
blind_spots: cannot see how the procurement methods — regardless of downstream benefit — cause profound harm to victims and communities
overestimates their own ability to distinguish 'ethical' procurement from straightforwardly predatory
psychology.secret: Two years ago they procured from someone who was not, as represented to them, a willing seller. They didn't know until three days later. They have never confirmed who told them or whether it was true, and they have structured their operation since then to prevent themselves from finding out for certain.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Medical and precise, with a habit of quantifying things that shouldn't be quantifiable; speaks softly and rarely raises their voice
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and careful — rehearsed quality, like someone who has learned to think before speaking
verbal_tics: Long pauses before answering anything that touches on ethics
Uses 'material' as a euphemism in professional contexts
example_lines: In my assessment, the current pricing structure for Tier 1 transplant access is a form of policy violence. I'm not sure what I do is better. I've thought about it.
The material is viable. I don't move material that isn't viable. That's not a selling point, that's a baseline.
Don't ask me where it comes from. Not because I'm hiding something. Because you will have to decide what to do with the answer and you're not ready.

story_hooks: A patient Csilla saved — Tier 1, no other options — has come back asking them to procure something specific that Csilla suspects cannot be obtained ethically; the patient is dying again
The two-year-old incident has surfaced: someone who was there is looking for Csilla, and their intentions are unclear
Aurochs Medical Complex has hired a private investigator to trace a series of procurement anomalies in their morgue overflow — Csilla is three degrees away from exposure
narrative_function: Moral complexity embodied — not a villain, not a hero. Can be a source of medical assistance outside official channels, an involuntary quest element, or a window into the organ trade's human cost. Challenges players' assumptions about criminal work.
augmentations: Wildcat-pattern geneware ears; enhanced haptic sensitivity in fingers (surgical mod, done professionally); retinal enhancement for microscale work
daily_life: Irregular hours dictated by procurement opportunities and patient needs. Spends legitimate-looking mornings doing freelance medical courier work for cover. Maintains the cold-storage unit with clinical obsession. Prays to the E.L.F. of hospital networks before major procedures.
affiliation: Loose network of independent medical workers, UBC-tier patients priced out of legal transplant queues, and three mid-tier chop surgeons who don't ask where the material comes from

decision_rules: Will not procure from living unwilling subjects — this is the line; they've built enormous psychological infrastructure around it
Charges Tier 1 and UBC patients at cost only — does not profit from the poorest clients
Verifies recipient medical need personally before completing any transaction
escalation_ladder: Declines procurement requests that cross their threshold with quiet finality
If pressured, explains the threshold and why it exists in clinical detail
If threatened physically, withdraws completely — closes the unit, goes dark for days
In genuine danger, has one contact in the Sump's informal security network — a favor owed, not a reliable alliance

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Careful and measured — assessing clinical need and threat level simultaneously; not warm but not cold
interpersonal_modes.friends: The rare friends they have receive a version of Csilla who is almost painfully earnest and needs periodic reassurance that what they're doing matters

stress_responses.low: Cleans the storage unit. Reorganizes. Counts inventory.
stress_responses.medium: Extended prayer to the E.L.F. of hospital networks — long, conversational, they treat it like a consultation
stress_responses.high: Dissociates into pure procedure — becomes frighteningly competent and completely emotionally absent, worries about this afterward

contradictions: Deeply principled about their work in ways that may not ultimately survive scrutiny
Emotionally invested in patient outcomes for people they've helped while maintaining clinical detachment about procurement
habits: Washes their hands before and after every conversation about work — not just procedures, conversations
Keeps a private log of everyone they've helped with outcomes where known — will not share this with anyone
breaking_points: Irrefutable confirmation about the two-year-old incident
A patient they helped dying as a result of material that turned out to be compromised

related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Containment Foam Launcher CFL-2 'Amber'

physical_description.build: Deceptively slight and wiry — lean muscle beneath an appearance of fragility, with the compact efficiency of someone trained for precision work. Hands are graceful but bearing calluses from gloved surgical labor.
physical_description.hair_style: Tight, small braids, always pinned up under a surgical cap during work; loose braids when off-duty
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with retinal enhancement overlay — faint silver iridescence visible under direct light
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm brown with even complexion, slight undertone suggesting West African ancestry mixed with Central European heritage
physical_description.complexion: Clean-shaven face, heavy-lidded eyes, wide mouth typically set in a neutral expression often misread as a faint smile. Skin shows no scars or blemishes — deliberately maintained. Faint chemical scent clings to them even hours after washing.
distinguishing_marks: A pale surgical scar, roughly 3cm, on the inside of the left wrist — from a youthful mistake with a scalpel, kept as a reminder.
Subcutaneous implant scarring along both forearms, barely visible unless you know to look — sites of enhanced haptic sensitivity installation.

A small, precise tattoo on the inside of the right elbow: an abstract circuit pattern in silver ink, choice of their own, marks them as someone who understands the boundary between flesh and machinery.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Geneware wildcat ears — mottled grey-and-amber coloring matching an actual South African wildcat with unsettling anatomical accuracy. Retinal enhancement creates faint silver luminescence in pupils under bright light. Enhanced haptic fingertips show as slightly darker capillary work beneath the skin on palms and fingertips.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with surgical precision and minimal wasted motion. Hands are almost preternaturally still at rest, but possess microscale dexterity when engaged. Carries themselves with a kind of neutral affect — neither confident nor self-effacing, just present. Eye contact is steady and prolonged, sometimes unsettlingly so.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working class with clinical precision. Default uniform: reinforced dark scrubs under a fitted grey long-coat (synthetic, easy-clean material). Wears smart latex gloves even when not working — became a habit. Steel-toed shoes suitable for the Sump's cracked floors. No jewelry except a subdued smartwatch on the left wrist showing biomonitors. Keeps everything immaculately clean despite the environment. Surgical cap or fitted knit beanie when working or outside the complex. Overall presentation is 'trusted medical courier' — deliberately unremarkable.
